headline: MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigns after PM's directive over Raadda health center attack
summary: Reserved women's seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty submitted her resignation to the Speaker following Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's instruction, prompted by the demolition of the Raadda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur.
details: Reserved women's seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty has resigned following a directive from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Her resignation comes in the wake of the attack on the Raadda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur. The Speaker's office confirmed her resignation and declared her seat vacant.

The incident involved the demolition and looting of the Raadda MCH-FP Center, a mother and child healthcare facility, in Mirpur on September 24. Several individuals associated with local BNP politics were implicated in the attack.

This incident, along with others like attacks on New Guinea Properties and Salman Muktadir's studio, and attempts to occupy buildings in Adabor and Mohammadpur, sparked widespread criticism regarding law and order. These events raised questions about the government's control over the situation.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took a strong stance upon returning from the UN General Assembly, gathering information and consulting advisors on the Raadda incident. He sought advice on taking exemplary organizational and legal action.

The Prime Minister's move is seen as a clear message to party workers: political identity will not shield them from criminal or irregular activities. The resignation of a party MP and the expulsion of others underscore this commitment to discipline.

Prior to Misty's resignation, the Dhaka North BNP and Juba Dal, along with Dhaka West Chhatra Dal committees, were dissolved. Additionally, 14 individuals from BNP, Chhatra Dal, Swechchasebak Dal, and Sramik Dal were expelled from their respective organizations for their alleged involvement.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that no one who violates party discipline or engages in immoral and reprehensible activities will be spared. The Election Commission has announced that a by-election for the vacant seat must be held within 90 days.

headline_marked: [[Expelled Jubo Dal leader taken into custody]] after Banglamotor altercation leaves man injured
headline: Expelled Jubo Dal leader taken into custody after Banglamotor altercation leaves man injured
summary: A 45-year-old man was injured during an altercation with an expelled Jubo Dal leader in Dhaka’s Banglamotor, sparking tension. Locals gathered, accusing the leader of extortion, and a motorcycle was later found on fire.
details: A 45-year-old man was injured during an altercation with an expelled Jubo Dal leader in Dhaka’s Banglamotor on Thursday night, sparking tension in the area.

The incident occurred around 8:10 PM in a lane on the northern side of Banglamotor, under Hatirjheel Police Station. Hatirjheel Police Station OC Md Asaduzzaman stated that neighbors Sohan and Ferdous Ahmed Simon, an expelled convener of Hatirjheel Thana Jubo Dal, became involved in an argument.
During the altercation, Sohan was struck on the head and sustained injuries. Police also received allegations that Simon later fired two blank rounds at the scene.
Following the incident, more than 100 locals gathered outside Simon’s home, chanting slogans and accusing him of extortion, expressing long-standing frustration with his activities.

Around 11:15 PM, a motorcycle was seen on fire beside the Banglamotor-Moghbazar road, with Fire Service personnel present. Police and SRB personnel were deployed as several locals alleged law enforcers were protecting Simon.
A local resident, Sohail, stated that people in the area had long been fed up with Simon’s alleged extortion, claiming he had "ruined the environment in the area."
Around midnight, police escorted Simon out of his residence and took him into custody. OC Asaduzzaman confirmed the development, stating that legal proceedings were underway.
